name: West Ridge
approach: From the Esmeralda Basin/Longs Pass Trailhead (end of Teanaway River Road/FS-9737, ~4,300 ft), take the Longs Pass Trail (FST 1391) roughly 2.3 miles and about 2,300 ft of gain to Longs Pass (~6,200 ft), a broad open saddle. From the pass, drop steeply down the north side (a boot path, with snow fingers usable for glissading in early season) about 1,300-1,400 ft to the Ingalls Creek drainage (~4,800 ft). Ford or rock-hop Ingalls Creek (can run high with early-season snowmelt) and pick up the Ingalls Creek Trail, following it right (east) about a half to full mile to the Beverly-Turnpike Trail junction. Leave the maintained trail here for a boot/climbers' path (sometimes called the "tapeworm trail") that switchbacks up through timber and brush before opening into meadow beneath Sherpa and Argonaut Peaks. Gain the rounded rib dividing the Cascadian Couloir drainage from the basin under Sherpa, then contour around 5,800 ft into the snow-holding basin below the West Ridge; kick steps up final snow/talus slopes to a common bivy/base-camp shelf around 7,400 ft (a flat table-rock area) or continue straight to the ridge base. Total gain from the car to the base of technical climbing runs roughly 3,400-4,700 ft depending on whether you camp or go car-to-car, with 6-7 hours of hiking typical for the one-way approach. Water is available at Ingalls Creek and from snowmelt in the upper basin in season; the brushy bushwhack down to Ingalls Creek and the long boulder/talus field beneath Sherpa are the main route-finding and stamina cruxes of the approach.

approach_variants.name: Esmeralda TH over Longs Pass and up from Ingalls Creek
approach_variants.notes:
Esmeralda Basin / Longs Pass Trailhead at the end of the North Fork Teanaway Road (FS-9737), about 4,300 ft. Longs Pass Trail (FST 1391) for roughly 2.3 miles and 2,300 ft to Longs Pass at about 6,200 ft.

Drop the north side, losing 1,300-1,400 ft to Ingalls Creek at about 4,800 ft — early season there are snow fingers here that glissade well. Ford or rock-hop the creek, join the Ingalls Creek Trail and follow it right (east) about a mile to the Beverly-Turnpike Trail junction at about 4,700 ft.

Leave the maintained trail there. Ascend rightward across the meadow to where the slope steepens at about 5,000 ft, cross the stream, and climb the rib staying left of its crest. At around 5,800 ft traverse right, cross over the rib, and contour into the basin below Sherpa.

There is a flat table-rock shelf at about 7,400 ft that parties use as a bivy or gear-up spot. Around 6,000 ft the climbers' path enters a spot where the gully narrows; from there some parties gain a few hundred feet east to the divide separating that gully from the one leading more directly toward Sherpa, then drop grudgingly into the correct gully and take class 2 slopes up to the table rock.

Six to seven hours one way is typical. Water at Ingalls Creek and from snowmelt in the upper basin in season.
approach_variants.season: mid-Jul-Sep; snow lingers on the approach benches and north-facing ground into early July
hazards: Steep loose drop off the north side of Longs Pass
Ingalls Creek ford runs high in early-season melt
Brushy bushwhack between the Ingalls Creek Trail and the open basin
Long boulder and talus field beneath Sherpa — a stamina and route-finding crux both
Picking the correct gully out of the basin: the obvious narrowing at ~6,000 ft is a decision point, not the line
Descent is rappels off mixed fixed slings, some reported as poor — carry cord
approach_variants.baseFinding:
The landmark that settles this route is Sherpa's balanced rock — a distinctive perched block on the summit ridge, and it is visible from the basin below. Use it.

From the basin at about 7,000 ft, climb a broad gully trending north-northeast to gain the ridge crest just east of the balanced rock. That is the correct point on the crest. From there the line runs westward over blocks and sandy benches, passing the balanced rock, to the summit — class 3-4.

So the check in cloud is: pick the crest, find the balanced block, and make sure it is to your west when you arrive. If the block is behind you to the east, you gained the crest too far along and are between the balanced rock and the summit rather than below it.

The flat table-rock at about 7,400 ft is the intermediate confirmation on the way up — it is a distinct flat platform in otherwise broken ground and it sits on the correct line. Do not confuse the table rock (7,400 ft, a bivy shelf) with the balanced rock (on the summit ridge, a perched block); they are different features doing different jobs.

The descent uses a rappel line back to a notch west of the technical climbing, so know where the notch is before you go up.

waypoints.name: Esmeralda Basin / Ingalls Lake Trailhead (N Fork Teanaway River Rd)
waypoints.directions: Drive the North Fork Teanaway River Road (FS-9737) to its end at the Esmeralda Basin / Longs Pass trailhead, about 4,300 ft. The road is usually open to the trailhead by early June, but the route itself wants late June through September, once the Longs Pass approach and the rock are snow-free. From the lot take the Longs Pass Trail (FST 1391), which climbs roughly 2.3 miles and 2,300 ft to Longs Pass.

waypoints.name: Long's Pass
waypoints.directions: From the lot, follow the Esmeralda Basin trail 0.3 mile and turn right onto the Ingalls Way Trail (#1390). Climb about 1.4 miles to the junction at about 5,440 ft, turn right onto the Longs Pass trail, and switchback steeply up open, rocky slopes about 1.2 miles to the pass.

waypoints.name: Sherpa south basin camp
waypoints.directions: Drop steeply off the north side of the pass on the boot path, about 1,400 ft, to Ingalls Creek; ford or rock-hop it and follow the Ingalls Creek Trail east about a mile to the Beverly-Turnpike junction. Leave the trail on the climbers' path up through timber and brush, climb the rib staying left of its crest, and at about 5,800 ft traverse right over the rib into the basin below Sherpa.

waypoints.name: Base of west ridge
waypoints.directions: Climb class 2 snow and talus up the basin past the flat table-rock shelf at about 7,400 ft to the notch at the west foot of the ridge, on the col between Stuart and Sherpa; aim for the notch closest to Sherpa.

waypoints.name: Sherpa Peak summit
waypoints.directions: Climb blocky class 4 ridge trending climber's left to a cave belay, then take the crack out of the cave (the crux, about 5.4 to 5.5). Continue left to a platform with a rappel anchor, scramble across a short gully, climb to the lowest point of the summit ridge, and follow it on exposed class 4 to the summit block.

approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: From the Esmeralda Basin Trailhead at the end of the North Fork Teanaway Road (FR-9737), via the Ingalls Way Trail
